text:
Thomas Harley is playing 25 minutes a night for Dallas, and closer to 26 lately, and the production has followed the ice time. He has 13 points in 18 games and 10 in his last ten, with two assists against Winnipeg on Thursday. He is also doing the unglamorous part: 41 blocked shots already.

The scoring is running a little ahead of him. His 1.73 points per 60 is above the top of our range for him (1.67), and over those ten games he has 10 points against roughly 6.6 expected. But this is not a luck story in the usual sense: his shooting and the finishing around him are both close to normal. The points are coming because Dallas is creating more with him out there (53% of five-on-five expected goals, 3.4 points better than without him).

That matters, because Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, with chances against piling up. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 28% of his shots coming off the rush, high for a defenseman. Watch his defensive numbers: if those hold, this is a real step.
